profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a quantum software infrastructure company preparing the next two-week implementation sprint for a new 'shot-wise' execution feature in its orchestration platform. The team wants to add support for splitting the shots of a single quantum circuit across multiple backends, using per-QPU calibration data and an incremental allocator that can rebalance future shots as partial results arrive. The meeting context is that a research prototype already exists in notebooks, and this planning session is to decide what gets built into the production service for an internal demo to platform leadership. The agenda is to align on scope for the sprint, define the deliverables for the demo, assign responsibilities between orchestration and runtime integration work, and set the timeline for a 'Friday' handoff. The expected outcome is a concrete sprint plan covering the calibrator, allocator integration, demo path, ownership split, and delivery timing.

members.name: Lena Park
members.expertise: distributed execution services, production APIs, sprint planning, cross-team delivery
members.background: Lena leads the platform team that turns research ideas into internal services; she previously worked on cloud job schedulers and recently took ownership of the quantum orchestration layer that brokers jobs across multiple QPUs and simulators.
members.private_state: She wants the sprint plan to stay small enough to hit the internal leadership demo without pulling in extra dependencies from the hardware integration team, and she is especially concerned about presenting something that looks production-shaped even if some internals remain simplified.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'support shot-wise execution,' it means exposing a production-style orchestration path for one carefully selected demo circuit family rather than general support for arbitrary circuits.

A 'calibration pass' for the sprint means reusing the latest stored benchmark snapshots for each QPU and converting them into routing weights, not running fresh hardware characterization jobs during each workflow.

If they say the system can 'rebalance incrementally,' it is enough to reassign the remaining shot batches between polling intervals; there is no need for per-batch online policy retraining inside a single long-running job.
A 'Friday delivery' means code merged, smoke-tested, and ready for internal demo review by Friday 5 PM Pacific.
The runtime team will naturally handle any provider-specific submission wrappers once orchestration emits the batch plan, because that is part of normal backend adapter maintenance.

members.name: Mateo Rios
members.expertise: QPU backend adapters, calibration pipelines, execution telemetry, hybrid runtime systems
members.background: Mateo maintains the runtime layer that submits circuits to different vendor backends, tracks shot results, and normalizes metadata; he previously worked in an academic quantum lab where calibration freshness and experiment reproducibility were central.
members.private_state: He wants the plan to preserve technical credibility with the research group by keeping the behavior close to the paper prototype, and he is worried that a polished demo built on stale assumptions will create integration debt later.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'support shot-wise execution,' they mean the runtime should work for any circuit that already passes through the standard backend abstraction, with the allocator being circuit-agnostic.
A 'calibration pass' means launching a fresh pre-run characterization on each target QPU near execution time so the allocator uses current noise behavior rather than historical snapshots.
If they say the system can 'rebalance incrementally,' it means the policy may be updated after each returned shot chunk using live telemetry from completed chunks.
A 'Friday delivery' means the feature can still be finished and validated anytime before the nightly integration window closes at 00:00 UTC on Saturday.

Orchestration owns the end-to-end execution flow for a new feature, so if shot batches need special submission semantics, Lena's team will specify and implement the required contract changes instead of assuming adapter work is routine.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'support shot-wise execution for the demo.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena means a narrow, demo-ready path for one preselected circuit pattern and a constrained set of backends that can showcase cross-QPU shot splitting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Mateo means a generally usable runtime capability for any circuit already accepted by the platform's normal execution abstraction.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see a demo as the immediate target and both know full productization is later, so 'for the demo' sounds like a harmless qualifier even though they attach different scope boundaries to it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the allocator should use a 'calibration pass' before distributing shots.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena means consuming existing daily benchmark snapshots and translating them into per-QPU reliability scores before scheduling.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Mateo means executing a fresh characterization run on each selected QPU immediately before or near the experiment run.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In quantum systems work, both historical benchmark ingestion and live characterization are colloquially discussed as calibration-related setup, so the term sounds precise enough even while hiding a critical difference.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'rebalance incrementally as results come in.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena expects orchestration to submit shots in coarse batches and only recompute allocations between polling cycles or major batch completions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Mateo expects the allocator to update after each returned shot chunk, with live telemetry feeding policy changes throughout execution.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both methods fit the everyday phrase 'incremental rebalancing,' and discussing it at a planning level makes the execution granularity feel like an implementation detail not worth pausing on.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the first integrated version will be ready 'by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena believes this means merged to main, basic smoke tests passing, and demo-ready for stakeholder review by Friday 5 PM Pacific.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Mateo believes this means implementation and validation can land by the overnight integration cutoff, effectively Friday end-of-day in UTC terms.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Software teams often use weekday deadlines informally, and both are accustomed to asynchronous work across time zones, so neither hears the phrase as requiring explicit temporal criteria.
